verdict: distinct_agencies (keep both; AR063019E footprint must move off the statewide overlay to Hot Springs Village)
rationale: The roster settles identity — AR063019E is Hot Springs Village PD spanning Garland and Saline, and the panel's own county field (051 Garland) differs from Benton's Saline (125), so there is no twin relationship with AR0630100 to dedupe. The load-bearing defect is the footprint: the fallback_overlap onto the Arkansas statewide layer smears a gated community's 44 counts across the entire state, and they belong on the Hot Springs Village CDP polygon, split across the Garland/Saline line rather than assigned to either county whole. On the peer-floor screen, first-NIBRS-year status is the wrong exemption criterion here because AR063019E reported a full 12 months — the low 277 per 100k is genuine, driven by HSV being a gated retirement community whose age structure makes the 1,326 peer median inapplicable. Exempt partial first years and compare against demographically matched peers; do not exempt on first-year status alone.

verdict: same_agency_merge / superseded_ori — CA010M100 superseded by CA010015M (kill the 245.3 fill); CA0100100 distinct and unaffected
rationale: Clovis is trivially separate: exclusive footprint on place 0614218, 127,560 population, a 2,437 series with no relation to either hospital ORI. The two hospital ORIs carry the identical name, the same Fresno county, and strictly non-overlapping active windows — CA010M100 runs SRS through 2020 then falls silent, CA010015M starts NIBRS in 2022, with 2021 empty as a transition gap — which is the canonical superseded-ORI signature, and there is only one Coalinga State Hospital with one DSH police force. The 229→42 magnitude drop is explained by the SRS-to-NIBRS lane change at a forensic psychiatric facility plus census reduction, not by a second unit. The disposition is robust either way: an ORI silent four years and absent from the 2024 roster must not receive a hist_median fill, and here that fill is 239.8 fabricated aggravated assaults stacked on top of the 42 real counts CA010015M already reports.

verdict: distinct_agencies (keep all six for 2024; CA0349900 is a post-2021 RESIDUAL, not a container)
rationale: Arithmetic kills the container hypothesis outright: a rollup cannot be smaller than its largest member, and CA0349900's 191 is far below North Sacramento's 1,554. The mass-migration reading is confirmed by continuity across the break — the 2020 county rollup of 2,734 versus the 2024 six-ORI group total of 2,671, with the 2-month 2021 startup annualizing to ~3,588 — and CA0349900's 2024 vector (0/0/0/1/0/76/114) is no subset of the area offices' larceny (707) or MVT (1,758) sums. The two halves therefore mean different things: pre-2021 CA0349900 is the whole-county CHP aggregate, post-2021 it is a thin county-office residual, so the series must be broken at 2021 for any trend or hist_median use. The real duplication is the ~30 sibling counties where a zero-reporting CA0xxx9900 draws a fabricated fill off pre-2021 rollup history — that fill re-adds mass the area offices already carry and must be suppressed; the w=1.0 statewide-overlay smear of all six is a separate, genuine footprint defect.

verdict: same_agency_merge — canonical FL0529900, footprint Seminole place 1264975; sub-question (3) SPUB 1181 vs FBI 397 = unclear_escalate
rationale: The trailing 'X' is stated to be the pipeline's own NIBRS-lane variant marker, so FL052990X is not an independent ORI9 at all; its 2021-2024 NIBRS values being exactly FL0529900's SRS values, and its FBI population being 19,300 (Seminole's size, not Largo's 85,000), confirm one agency whose roster row simply landed on the synthetic twin — which is also why FL0529900 reads as roster-absent. The LARGO panel name and the crosswalk to place 1239425 are both wrong; Largo has its own department and would never produce 397 counts. On value selection I decline to rule: because the X twin is synthetic, SRS and NIBRS are one submission rather than two agreeing sources, and the SPUB ratios are strongly non-uniform (robbery 3→25 = 8.3x against burglary 32→50 = 1.6x), which rules out a clean counting-convention scalar and leaves scope difference versus FBI under-submission genuinely undetermined. Escalating: 784 counts turn on it and Seminole's possible Pinellas County Sheriff contract status would change the answer.

verdict: same_agency_merge — MA0146400 + MA014640X are one agency (canonical MA0146400); MA014649E distinct and kept. Two agencies, not three. Partial-year uplift must NOT survive
rationale: The seven-year byte-identical series is conclusive when combined with the documented meaning of the 'X' suffix as the pipeline's NIBRS-lane variant marker: MA014640X is MA0146400's NIBRS lane, which is also why the roster row attached to the synthetic twin and left MA0146400 roster-absent. MA014649E is a genuinely separate stream — a different magnitude in every one of seven years (44/28/22/25/41/31/25) and a different county (027 Worcester versus 017 Middlesex) — so it is kept. The 5→15 uplift is clearly wrong and should be dropped: the same agency's NIBRS lane reports 12 months at exactly 5, proving the SRS '4mo' is an unpopulated months-reported field rather than a genuine partial year, so the estimator is tripling a complete observation. I do not resolve which Tufts campus each unit is (both roster rows read 'Tufts University: Worcester' with conflicting counties, and the Grafton/Cummings versus Medford-Somerville assignment is underdetermined) — that sub-question should escalate, though it is low-stakes at 5 and 25 counts, and neither campus unit belongs on the statewide overlay regardless.

verdict: same_agency_merge — one agency (Windsor PD); canonical CA0491300, footprint Windsor town place 0685922; suppress CA0491500's 2023-2024 CIUS rows
rationale: The panel names are stale and the FBI population field is decisive: CA0491500 carries Windsor's ~27,000 through 2019 then drops to 0, while CA0491300 carries 0 through 2019 then picks up 27,165 in 2020 and holds ~25,700 — a clean identity handoff in 2020, and a facility closed to residents in 2018 could never carry 27,165 people. That also explains the otherwise absurd jump of a shuttered institution to 272 counts in 2020: from 2020 the ORI stopped being Sonoma Developmental Center. Exact agreement on the full seven-vector in two consecutive years (230 and 248) is not a numeric coincidence, and the earlier reviewer's coincidence finding is an artifact of trusting panel names over population and lane structure. Net effect of the fix: 248 lands on Windsor town once and the statewide-overlay copy disappears; note CA0491300 is a recycled ORI whose pre-2020 SDC history must be severed, and the roster's CAL FIRE Sonoma-Lake-Napa label on CA0491500 may be a genuine later reassignment that does not affect the 2024 disposition.

verdict: distinct_agencies — both kept; MI1935000's 2024 value is its own lanes' 6 (partial-year adjusted to ~10), NOT the CIUS 128
rationale: The departments are genuinely separate — an incorporated city and the surrounding township, both roster-present — so the defect is value attribution, not identity. CIUS's 1/10/1/26/9/75/6 under the city ORI is byte-identical to DeWitt Township's own NIBRS and SRS vector, while the city's own lanes read 0/1/0/2/0/3/0; an exact seven-field match at that magnitude is misattribution, and 128 is also ~10x the city's entire 13-44 history against a 4,777 population. Taking CIUS double-counts the township's mass and erases the city's true value; the correct treatment is the city's own 6 at 7-8 months with a genuine partial-year uplift to roughly 10, which sits squarely in its 13-44 range next to 2023's 13. One rule handles the recurring Lincoln/Coloma/Montrose/Clayton pattern and is the same test that resolves the Windsor and River Falls cases: where a publication-lane vector for agency A exactly matches another agency B's own-lane vector in the same state and A's own lanes materially disagree, treat the publication row as misattributed and prefer A's own lanes — an exact-vector-collision test rather than a Michigan-specific patch.

Different counties ~150 miles apart, different crosswalk targets (cousub 3603911649 vs place 3613145), populations 6,671 vs 2,729, both continuously present under their own names on the 2024 roster with independent 7-year series, and the agreement is confined to 2024 (Cazenovia is NIBRS since 2023-04-01, Cairo has no NIBRS start). The shared vector 0/0/0/0/1/24/0 is the single most common shape a ~25-count small agency can take (all larceny plus one burglary), so equality carries almost no information, and DCJS prints 26 with 2 burglaries for Cazenovia versus 25 with 1 for Cairo, i.e. these are not the same underlying record. To reject this without losing River Falls / DeWitt / PSP York / Windsor, the screen must require a linking signal beyond vector equality: a name-token or jurisdictional relation (same county, nested or containing geography, overlapping crosswalk polygon) or complementary histories (one ORI's series ending where the other's begins, or one missing from the current roster). A second criterion does the same work: require agreement in two or more years, or require vector entropy (nonzero in three-plus offense categories) rather than a single all-larceny total, which kills low-N coincidences while every genuine duplicate in the batch still passes.

verdict: same_agency_merge — canonical PAPSP9400; PA067SP00 is the superseded twin, its pre-2021 history stitched onto PAPSP9400
rationale: Pennsylvania State Police maintain one UCR reporting unit per county, and these two carry the same county, the same statewide-overlay footprint, and byte-identical 2024 vectors (0/3/3/58/1/256/6). The 2023 discrepancy of 2 is affirmative evidence rather than against: exact agreement in 2021, 2022 and 2024 with a two-count drift in one year is the signature of one submission pulled at two refresh times, whereas two genuinely distinct units would never track at 603/310/327. PAPSP9400 is canonical for 2024 because it is the roster-present, NIBRS-lane record; PA067SP00's 2018-2020 history (649/598/199) must be carried forward as PAPSP9400's baseline rather than left as a standalone agency, or PSP York loses its pre-2021 series and PA067SP00 becomes a fill candidate. Consistent cross-link rule for d-PAPSP2500-erie: 2024 roster presence decides canonicity per county in whichever direction it points — never a blanket preference for either ORI family — and the silent off-roster twin receives no fabricated fill in either direction, because the live twin is already reporting that mass.

verdict: same_agency_merge / superseded_ori — canonical WI0561100; WI0480100 retired; the 170 counts belong on River Falls city place 5568275
rationale: One department whose ORI moved blocks: River Falls straddles the Pierce/St. Croix line, Wisconsin assigns ORI blocks by county, and WI0480100's own FBI lanes stop dead in 2020 exactly as WI0561100's begin in 2021 — with CIUS's 113/181/170 for 2022-2024 under the retired ORI matching WI0561100's own-lane values exactly, so these are the same incidents, not additional mass. WI0561100 is roster-present as River Falls PD with a matching 17,171 population. On the place: 5568275 is correct and 5563100 is a first_pass misplacement, because Wisconsin place FIPS run alphabetically and River Falls must sort after Racine (~5566000) — 5563100 falls before it, so the retired ORI's crosswalk should be inherited rather than the live ORI's guess (worth confirming against the place file). General rule for a publication lane still emitting under a retired ORI: resolve ORI identity BEFORE applying lane precedence, and suppress any CIUS/SPUB row on an off-roster ORI whose vector matches a live ORI's own lanes — otherwise publication precedence resurrects dead agencies and doubles their mass.

The same agency-year carries 23 Part-I counts in the SRS lane (0/0/1/10/1/6/5), so the FDLE full-year zero is factually false, and a zero year for the FHP troop covering Hillsborough/Tampa is implausible on its face. Believe SRS: positive observations cannot be un-observed by a blank cell rendered as 0 with a default 12-month label. Operationally the year is neither zero nor complete — 23 counts at 1 month reported, consistent with the agency's intermittent 1-month history (35 at 1mo in 2020, 5 at 1mo in 2023) — so it should be treated as missing/partial and imputed, never published as observed 0. This matters more than usual because the footprint is 12:statewide_overlap_layer, so a false zero smears across the whole state.

CIUS carries affirmative 12-month zeros in four separate years (2018, 2022, 2023, 2024) for an FBI-population-0 campus force whose entire seven-year panel is zero in every lane, with no competing positive count anywhere — that is a stable zero-reporter, not a blank cell read as 0. Exposure makes zero cheap: a small Milledgeville campus department has a non-trivial probability of a genuinely empty Part-I year, exactly the exception any 'positive history implies gap' rule must carve out. Pipeline-local verdict: true_zero. General principle for the ~250 zero-history CIUS full-year zeros: accept only when (a) no other lane carries a positive count for that agency-year, (b) peer-implied expected Part-I count is small (roughly <3), which in practice means population-0 special-jurisdiction forces and sub-1,000 places, and (c) the zero recurs across non-adjacent years; everything else escalates rather than auto-accepting — and note the opposite default applies to the 897 of 1,211 CIUS all-zero agency-years that do have positive history.

The 12-month CIUS zero is affirmative on its face, but 2024 is this agency's debut row (2018-2023 are SRS 0-month absences, i.e. missing, not observed zeros), so there is no prior behaviour to separate a real zero-reporter from an onboarding shell — and the roster's NIBRS start of 2023-01-01 produced no NIBRS lane row in 2023 or 2024, keeping 'enrolled but silent' fully live. Exposure cuts the opposite way from Georgia Military College: 1,417 residents at the peer median of 702/100k implies about 10 expected Part-I offenses, where a true zero is unlikely, whereas GMC is a population-0 campus with four corroborating zero years. The facts that would settle it — whether Waterman PD actually filed twelve monthly zero-reports, and whether it is full-service or a part-time department that refers calls to the DeKalb County sheriff — are outside this panel. Escalate: do not accept the zero on the GMC precedent, and do not impute ~10 offenses onto a village on a peer median alone.

A growing 5,126-person exurb that posted 24/22/26/21/16 through 2022 cannot plausibly record zero Part-I offenses of every type in a real 12-month year. The agency has been a NIBRS reporter since 2020-06-01 yet is entirely absent from the NIBRS lane in 2024 with SRS at only 2 months — a reporter dropping out of its own submission channel is a non-reporting signature, not a quiet year. Yes, 2023 should be flagged alongside 2024: 1 count on 11 NIBRS months against a 16-26 baseline is the same defect a year earlier, it just lands as a token/zero-report rather than an all-zero row, so the b2 rule should look back one year and hand 2023 to the token screen rather than accepting it as observed.

Six consecutive years at months_reported = 0 is not a run of observed zeros, it is a record of never having submitted; and the 2024 SRS row covers 3 months, so the DCJS '12 months' is not backed by twelve months of returns. Total absence of any positive value in any lane in any year is therefore evidence about the reporting relationship, not about crime: at the peer median of 702/100k a 1,437-person village expects roughly 10 Part-I offenses a year, and a legitimately reporting small agency would have surfaced positives somewhere across seven years. The plausible benign story — a part-time village PD whose reports are taken by the Dutchess County Sheriff or NYSP — still does not license publishing an observed 0 against an exclusive w=1 village polygon; it argues for treating the cell as missing and revisiting coverage. Medium rather than high because the own-history arm is genuinely blind here and the call rests on the non-submission record plus a peer benchmark.

CIUS prints 12-month zeros for 2022, 2023 and 2024 while the submission record shows months_reported = 0 for 2022 and 2023 and only 2 months for 2024 — publication without submission, the blank-as-zero signature. The 2021 SRS 0-month row is a national artifact (Cairo and Cazenovia show it too), but 2022-2023 are agency-specific, since those same NY comparators do carry real month coverage in 22 and 23. A 9,153-population town with an active PD cannot post three consecutive true zeros across all seven categories; even the agency's own prior values (5, 7, 1) are far below a peer expectation near 60/yr, which points to chronic under-capture ending in outright non-reporting rather than a stable true zero. Confidence is medium rather than high only because West Point has its own force and the town's own historic rate is so low that a single genuine zero year would not be shocking — three in a row is.

The agency reported 13 counts in 5 months of 2022 and 24 in 8 months of 2023; a genuine 12-month zero the next year is arithmetically untenable for a 3,754-person borough with its own department (Poisson probability of zero at that rate is effectively nil). The 2024 SRS row shows months_reported = 0, so CIUS's '12 months' is a default label applied to a blank rather than a verified full year of returns. The eroding coverage sequence 12/10/11/absent/5/8 is the signature of a failing reporting relationship terminating in non-submission, which is exactly the generative process for a false published zero — the shrinking months make the zero less credible, not more.

Bellefonte is a 5,888-population county seat with an active borough PD that reported 31, 20 and 32 counts in 2018-2020; two consecutive CIUS 12-month zeros both sit on SRS rows with months_reported = 0, i.e. published without any submission behind them. The 2021-2022 collapse (2 counts at 1 month, then 3 at 3 months) makes the zeros LESS believable, not more: it documents a reporting relationship degrading toward non-submission, which is precisely the path that produces blank-as-zero cells. A zero arriving after a run of clean 12-month coverage would be the credible case; this is the opposite, and both 2023 and 2024 should be treated as missing and imputed.

This agency demonstrates the artifact on itself in 2018: CIUS printed a 12-month zero while SRS carried only 1 month of coverage, so the '12mo' label is a default, not a measurement. 2024 repeats it with SRS at 0 months after three fully absent years (2021-2023), meaning nothing was submitted for the year CIUS publishes as complete. The hist_median of 38 is worthless as a trigger — it rests on one 8-month year, and the 2019 row (0 at 10 months) shows this agency can genuinely report near-zero — but the decision does not need it: a 663-person borough PD with four straight years of no submission is more likely defunct or part-time with PSP coverage than truly crime-free. Treat as missing and route the defunct-agency question separately; do not publish an observed 0.

The 2018 row is a demonstrated false zero in this exact lane for this exact agency — CIUS published 0 at 12 months while NIBRS and SRS both recorded 24 — so the lane's full-year zeros for Castleton carry no evidentiary weight on their own. In 2024 NIBRS is absent entirely despite continuous NIBRS coverage since 1999, and SRS covers 2 months, so nothing supports a complete year. The 22 -> 6 -> 3 -> 0 decline with the NIBRS feed dropping out reads as a department winding down or cut to part-time, common in Vermont with coverage reverting to VSP; that is a fourth story, but it does not make the cell a true zero. Treat 2024 as missing, and if the wind-down is confirmed, reassign the town's exclusive w=1 polygon to the covering agency rather than publishing an observed 0.

The agency's own startup rate calibrates it: 18 counts in the 2 months after the 2021-11-01 start is ~9/month, which annualizes to ~108 and matches 2022 (102) and 2023 (101) exactly, so the real level is ~100/year and 8 is roughly one month of output. The family pattern is decisive against a crime explanation — Hanford 88 to 1 and Yreka 59 to 16 in the same year as SLO 101 to 8; three area offices do not simultaneously lose 85-99% of highway Part-I incidents, but they do share one central CHP submission path. Carry: ~1 believable month for CA0409945, and yes, treat the CHP area-office family under a single rule keyed to the shared submitter — detect the 2024 family-wide drop once and apply a common disposition, since with FBIpop 0 the per-ORI peer arm is blind but the family gives a within-family benchmark that works. Cross-check against a2-CA03499 before fixing the family roster.

Same mechanism as Lee County: SPUB 63 is 4.1% of the 2021-2023 baseline while SRS carries a complete 12-month 1,392 flush with 2022 (1,588) and 2023 (1,531), and the roster's nibrs_start of 2025-01-01 means FDLE's FIBRS extract could not have held Bay's 2024 volume. The near-agreement between the fill (1,533.3) and the discarded observation (1,392) is coincidence dressed as validation — the fill is built from the agency's own trend, the same information that makes 1,392 plausible, so agreement is expected and confirms nothing independently. It is also only aggregate-level: the filled row keeps SPUB's murder 0 against SRS 2, robbery 0 against 6 and MVT 3 against 63, so five of seven components are wrong while the total reads fine, exactly the failure a total-only check misses. Carry SRS 1,392 with its offense split; pipeline-local verdict data_error on the SPUB row.

SPUB 258 is 4.4% of the agency's own 2021-2023 baseline while the SRS lane carries a complete 12-month 5,776 for the same ORI, flush with 2022 (5,912) and 2023 (6,355); the SPUB offense shape (1/47/3/20/12/145/30) preserves the real mix at roughly 1/22 scale, the signature of a fragment rather than a crime collapse. Pipeline-local verdict: token_report_treat_as_partial, but the repair is lane selection, not uplift. Yes, SRS 5,776 should have beaten SPUB 258 — source_provenance.py ranks state publication above SRS unconditionally, and the roster's nibrs_start of 2025-01-01 shows Lee was not a FIBRS submitter during 2024, so FDLE's FIBRS offense-detail extract cannot hold its year; the 'months_reported = 12' label comes from the source sheet, not from evidence. And no, 7,187.8 is not defensible: it overshoots the discarded observation by 24%, and fabricating a value larger than an observation you threw away is strictly worse than using it. Carry SRS 5,776 with its own offense split.

Two Part-I offenses for a ~70,000-student campus against a complete SRS 12-month 207 that is the highest value in the agency's own series and consistent with 2022 (196) and 2023 (167); with nibrs_start 2025-01-01 the SPUB row is the same FIBRS fragment as the other Florida cases, so pipeline-local verdict is data_error and the panel should carry SRS 207 — no fill needed once the lane choice is corrected. On the blind spot: it does not need a population rule, it needs a population-free rule. A cross-lane disagreement screen — flag any ORI-year where two lanes both published at 12 months differ by more than about 3x — catches UCF, Lee, Bay and North Port without consulting population at all, and fires before the peer-rate arm is ever reached. Building enrolment/ridership/bed exposure proxies for the 4,133 zero-population ORIs is far more work for less yield; what survives the disagreement screen is the single-lane, no-history case (Waterman), which is properly a review item rather than a rule.

335 is 6.8% of the 2018-2023 median with the offense mix intact (0/13/6/52/52/196/16, larceny-dominant) — the same shape-preserving magnitude collapse as the other FDLE rows, and 6.8% is about 0.8 of a month, so pipeline-local verdict is token_report_treat_as_partial with roughly one month believed. The missing 2024 SRS lane makes the diagnosis no harder, since it rests on own history and the sheriff peer rate (107.5 vs 964), neither of which needs a second lane; it makes the repair less precise, because the value must now be modelled rather than lifted from an observation. Carry an imputed figure anchored on own history and growth: hist_median 4,946.5 as a floor, or about 5,700 if the 2020 rate (4,706 at 257,516) is carried to the 2024 population of 311,569. The deeper defect this case exposes is that no fill fired at all — Lee got 6 offenses filled, Bay 3, North Port 1, Osceola 0 — because fill is decided per offense against per-offense thresholds instead of once at agency-year level after the year is judged a token report.

Seven Part-I offenses (0/3/0/0/0/4/0) for 93,930 residents — 0.8% of the 898 baseline, 7.5 per 100k against a peer median of 1,953 — sitting beside a complete SRS 12-month 822 means the SPUB row is a fragment, not a year. The mechanism is readable in the roster and the loader: North Port's nibrs_start is 2025-03-01, so it was a summary reporter throughout 2024 and FDLE's FIBRS offense-detail extract holds only its earliest partial/test NIBRS transmissions; load_fdle_annual_ags_rows admits any agency with quarters_reported >= 1, observations.py then takes the sheet's own period label to months_reported = 12 / tier high, and source_provenance.py ranks state publication above SRS. Carry SRS 822 — the 644.1 fill is wrong twice over, since it lifted larceny alone to 641.1 and left murder, robbery, burglary and MVT at the fragment's zeros, producing a row no reading supports. Pipeline-local verdict: data_error; the systemic fix is to gate the ladder on evidenced completeness (never let a lane win when a same-year 12-month lane for the same ORI is more than ~3x larger) instead of on lane identity.

The 49 is 23 murders plus 25 rapes plus 1 aggravated assault with zero robbery, burglary, larceny and motor vehicle theft — no city of any size produces that shape, so this is an offense-coverage failure, not low crime. The three-lane agreement is not independent corroboration: CIUS and the SRS rollup both derive from the same FBI submission for an agency whose roster nibrs_start is 2024-01-01, so all three lanes inherit one incomplete first-NIBRS-year feed; the start date wins. Pipeline-local verdict: structural_zero_treat_as_missing, and I would not preserve murder 23 / rape 25 as observed either — a feed that dropped every property segment gives no assurance it carried twelve months of persons offenses. Carry the ~5,580 hist_median fill as least-bad but flag it low-confidence, and separately flag the population: 241,780 is the pre-split Savannah-Chatham metro figure while the crosswalk footprints the ORI on Savannah city (place 1369000), so the baseline the fill leans on may describe a larger jurisdiction than the one being estimated.

Same signature as Taos: NIBRS claims 12 months while SRS carries the identical single count over 1 month, and that lone offence is a larceny — one property crime for an entire rural county of 12,729 for a full year is not a possible crime outcome for a sheriff's office that was still on the active roster. The peer arm alone would be sufficient here: 7.9 per 100k against a 630 sheriff-band median is 1.3% of peer, an implausibility that does not depend on the stale 2018 baseline at all, so the weakness of a single usable full year five years back does not change the ruling. Carry: ~1 believable month; because own history is one stale year, the fill should be peer-band anchored (10k-25k sheriff median applied to 12,729, roughly 80 counts) with the 2018-2019 values used only as a sanity bound, not as the point estimate.

The two hypotheses the case poses are both live and the evidence does not separate them. Against a reporting failure: both lanes show near-full submission (NIB 12mo, SRS 11mo), unlike the true token cases in this batch where SRS collapses to 1 month, and the 2024 mix is agg-assault-led (14) rather than the larceny-led shape a truncated school-district feed would show — that pattern fits a referral/handling policy change or an SRO transfer to Columbus PD. Against a real level: the whole series is erratic (7, 97, 517, 495, 956) so the 2021-2023 median of 517 is not a trustworthy anchor either, and FBIpop 0 blinds the peer arm entirely with no CIUS/SPUB lane to arbitrate. Panel should carry: do not fill toward 517 under either hypothesis, keep 30 recorded with a flag, and resolve by checking the 2024 GA state submission and whether the district still fields sworn officers — the mass sits on the statewide overlay so the cost of leaving it pending is low.

Smoothness is not evidence of authenticity — progressive RMS/NIBRS mapping loss decays gradually, and the decline here accelerates precisely after the 2020-08-01 conversion (-9%, -20%, -39%, -43%, -48%), with the 2020 NIBRS row already showing 120/6mo against SRS 293/12mo, i.e. the new lane was lossy from day one. The absolute-plausibility test is what should carry the ruling rather than the step size: 5 burglaries and 28 larcenies for a full year in a 13,872-population Indiana city, when the same agency's pre-conversion level was ~2,250 per 100k, is not a reachable crime outcome. What separates this from North Augusta is only the shape (compounding decay versus one cliff after a mild trend); the diagnosis is the same and North Augusta is the more confident of the two because its 2 burglaries are starker. Carry: roughly 2-4 months' equivalent of coverage; fill peer-anchored or from the 2018-2020 pre-conversion level, not from the already-decayed 2021-2023 median.

The months evidence separates this from the true tokens in this batch: SRS shows 16 counts across 10 actual monthly submissions (1.6/month) rather than the 1-month collapse seen at Taos and Emanuel, so the agency was reporting most of the year at a genuinely low rate — a 10-month uplift puts it near 19 against an own-history band of 41-77. The peer arm is invalid here and should not be used: the case's own context (KSP handles rural patrol) is confirmed by the fact that this sheriff's normal ~350 per 100k already sits well below the 630 band median, so the 17.4%-of-peer reading is a benchmark-mismatch artifact, not a deficit. The drop is larger than Poisson noise, so it is not nothing — but with ~40 counts at stake on a nonmunicipal remainder footprint, a per-case review should not be spent here. Default for the low-mass tail: apply the mechanical partial-month uplift where a lane disagrees on months, leave the value recorded and unfilled, and route to human review only above an absolute-mass threshold.

An exact zero across all seven Part-I categories, in the agency's first-ever panel appearance, with nibrs_start exactly 2024-01-01 and an SRS lane showing 0/0mo, is the canonical first-year administrative zero-report signature; the peer floor gives E = 702/100k x 1,638 = 11.5 expected offenses, so P(0) under the peer rate is ~1e-5. Critically, partial-year uplift is multiplicative and cannot rescue a zero, so 'treat as N believable months' is the wrong sub-disposition here — no month count changes the answer. Both competing real-world stories (first-year zero-reporting, or MSP/part-time coverage recording Colrain's crime under a different ORI) imply the same thing: the 0 does not measure crime in Colrain's territory, and accepting it manufactures exactly the absence-as-zero municipal control that docs/STATE.md line 429-445 already identifies as the Class A pathology (3,053 of 14,084 municipal jurisdictions carrying a zero total control). RULE for the 48 no-own-history agencies: bifurcate on zero vs nonzero. Exact all-category zeros published as complete years by agencies with no own history are treated as MISSING and routed to the benchmark-constrained silent-territory path (src/crimerisk/benchmark_imputation.py), never published as a measured zero control. Nonzero totals are accepted as credible low crime unless E = peer_rate x pop/1e5 is large AND the shortfall is many-sigma; where E is single-digit the peer floor has essentially no power and must not fire. First-NIBRS-year status is never evidence of low crime in either direction — mark year 1 provisional.

35 counts for New England's second-largest city — 16 murder, 17 aggravated assault, zero larceny — against a flat 4,700-5,250 series through 2022 and a roster showing no coverage change (NIBRS since 1995) is a broken feed, not crime. Pipeline-local verdict: structural_zero_treat_as_missing for the whole row; months_believed is the wrong frame (35 is about 9% of one normal month), and no component should be preserved — 17 aggravated assaults against a ~945 baseline proves the persons segments are incomplete too, so the estimator holding murder=16 and especially rape=0 as observations is itself a defect that publishes a 212k-population city with zero rapes. On 2023: handling 2,196 at 8 months as a partial year is procedurally right but the 12/8 uplift is wrong, since 2,196/8 = 275 per month against 2022's 391 means the reported months are already running ~70% of normal and the scaled year still understates by roughly a third. 2023 is best recorded as the first year of the same degradation — a partially-degraded partial — not a clean partial.

The 2024 row is internally impossible before any baseline comparison: 2 murders and 2 rapes alongside 0 robberies and 2 aggravated assaults cannot coexist — a city producing two homicides produces tens of aggravated assaults — so the violent-crime stream is passing while the assault and property streams are not. The 2022 calibration confirms the lane, not the agency: CIUS published 77 where NIBRS and SRS both had 649, an 8x publication error for this exact ORI, so CIUS/NIBRS agreement at 40 in 2024 is not corroboration. The whole post-2021 series (1,145 to 649 to 20 to 40) tracks the agency's 2021-01-01 NIBRS conversion, i.e. progressive transition loss, against a stable 1,145-1,248 for four prior years. Carry: 2024 is worth well under a month of coverage — treat as missing, fill from the pre-conversion level (~1,150-1,200, trend-adjusted for the 6% population decline), and mark 2022-2023 as unusable too.

The roster's NIBRS start of 2024-07-01 makes a 12-month NIBRS coverage claim arithmetically impossible — at most 6 months could exist — and the SRS lane independently reports the same single count over 1 month, so 1 month is the believable figure and 2 is the outside case. One aggravated assault as the entire Part-I output of a 25,860-population sheriff (3.9 per 100k against a peer median of 708) is not a crime fact; it is the first partial month of a conversion. The Taos municipal control (NM0290100) at 443 counts and 12 months in both lanes shows the county is not in a quiet year, and the sheriff's own 106-169 through 2020 sets the level. Carry: treat 2024 as ~1 month of coverage, suppress the published-complete flag, and impute from own pre-2021 history (~145) cross-checked against the sheriff peer band rather than uplifting 1 by 12.

Composition, not slope, settles the decline-versus-collapse question: the 2024 row shows 2 burglaries and 7 aggravated assaults for a growing 26,377-population South Carolina city that logged 615 in 2022, and no genuine trend takes burglary to 2 while larceny still carries 100 of the 117 total — that is a partial feed with one offense stream intact. The pre-existing monotonic decline (941 to 615 at roughly 10% a year) is real trend and should be honored, but it predicts roughly 400-500 for 2024, not 117; the 2023 value at 11 months and md tier suggests the decay had already begun in the submission pipeline. Roughly 2-4 months of 2024 are believable (117 against a ~35-50/month trend-adjusted expectation). Carry: flag as partial despite the three-lane 12-month agreement, and fill from the trend-extrapolated own-history level rather than the flat 2021-2023 median.

verdict: genuine_low_crime (credible_low_crime — accept 2, no uplift, no fill)
rationale: THE DISCRIMINATING FEATURE the rule must encode is proof-of-life of the reporting channel: any nonzero count demonstrates the channel can emit a nonzero, so the low value is a measurement; an exact all-category zero (Colrain) demonstrates nothing and is uninformative. Piute clears it twice over — 1 count in 2023 and 2 in 2024 form a coherent, stable two-year low sequence rather than a one-off, and the 2024 vector is specific (0/0/0/0/0/2/0, two larcenies) rather than a flat zero row. The peer arm is also structurally weak here: E = 595/100k x 1,607 = 9.6, and the sheriff peer median in the under-2,500 band is contaminated by sheriffs whose nominal population-served understates a large unincorporated patrol workload, whereas Piute is one of the genuinely least-populous counties in the US with ~1,600 total residents on the state_nonmunicipal_remainder. Blast radius is also 2 counts, so an accept error is immaterial while a Colrain-style accept error propagates a zero control. Secondary discriminators, in priority order after nonzero-ness: (2) more than one year of self-consistent low counts; (3) a specific rather than uniformly-zero offense vector; (4) E below ~10, where Poisson variation alone spans the observation.

2018-2021 is the correct reference: four consecutive full years at 18, 22, 24, 26 establish this division's true level, and 15 sits just under that band — the 170/130 of 2022-2023 is the anomaly the screen should be explaining, not the 2024 value. The SRS lane's 9 months for the same 15 counts would uplift to ~20, landing squarely inside the historical band, which independently corroborates the level. The mix (9 agg assault, 3 MVT, 1 robbery, 2 larceny) is the normal shape for a state police division with no resident population. Carry: no fill; and yes, a screen can catch this automatically — require the baseline window to be homogeneous (a level-shift/change-point test, or comparing the full-history median against the 3-year median and deferring to the longer series when they diverge) instead of hard-coding a 2021-2023 window.

verdict: defunct_no_fill — superseded_by CA0334900 (footprint succession, NOT organizational absorption)
rationale: The dates align exactly: CA0337800's last usable year is 2020 and CA0334900's first is 2021 with roster nibrs_start 2021-01-01, matching the 1 July 2020 handover from the Riverside County Sheriff's contract to the municipal Menifee PD; population passes 96,837 (2020) to 99,883 (2021) with no overlap, and both ORIs crosswalk w=1 exclusive to the identical place 0646842. On your superseded-vs-absorbed distinction: 'absorbed_by' is wrong because no larger continuing agency took this caseload onto its own book — the receiving entity is a brand-new municipal department covering exactly the same footprint, so this is footprint succession. That distinction has a concrete consequence you should encode: the two ORIs are continuous in TERRITORY but organizationally discontinuous (sheriff contract station vs municipal PD) and lane-discontinuous (SRS vs NIBRS), and the levels differ materially (~1,798-2,100 pre-2021 vs 1,149-1,883 after). So link them for place-level series continuity, but mark the 2020/2021 boundary as a hard break — CA0337800's counts must never be fed to CA0334900 as own-history for hist_median, trend_log_linear, or the Class C <0.35x own-history screen, or the 2024 drop to 1,149 will trip a false review. Drop the 1,747.4 fill; Menifee city 2024 = 1,149.

verdict: plausibly_active (ORI dormant_but_extant) — but no_fill AND remove from place allocation entirely
rationale: NPS and BLM unambiguously exist and retain federal law-enforcement officers, so this case proves roster-absence is a reporting fact, not an existence fact — yet extancy does not license the fill: a 3,071.8 hist_median built off a 2018-2020 base that went silent four years ago is fabrication regardless of whether the organization survives. The footprint is the larger error. This ORI is a NATIONAL aggregate stream with no county_fips and no place_fips; it reached the DC statewide overlay only via agency_master_fallback (review=fallback), and its overlap_subtype 'tribal' is self-evidently wrong for the National Park Service — that combination is a fallback artifact, not a geographic finding. ANSWER TO THE HARDER HALF: nationwide federal-land crime must not be allocated to any place-based denominator at all. It occurs on land whose visitor-generated incidents have no matching resident population in the denominator, so any allocation inflates a rate by construction; it should be carried as a separate non-allocated federal stratum, excluded from both the numerator pool and the control totals, and reported separately if reported at all. Allocating it correctly would require park-unit-level geography that the single national ORI cannot provide. Same disposition for DCDI00400 (BLM, 509.3). Unresolved and not needed for the disposition: whether a successor federal ORI now carries this stream — worth a CDE lookup, but it changes nothing here since neither ORI produced 2024 data.

The population handoff is dispositive and needs no external lookup: FL0160200 carries 920,508 in 2020 then 0 forever after, and FL0160000 carries 0 through 2020 then 920,385 in 2021 — a clean, non-overlapping baton pass of the same population at the same moment FL0160000's nibrs_start (2021-01-01) begins, which is an ORI re-key on the SRS-to-NIBRS transition, not two coexisting agencies. Jacksonville and Duval County have been a consolidated city-county since 1 October 1968 policed solely by the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, so a separate Jacksonville city PD reporting alongside a Duval sheriff never existed in this period; the 2024 roster confirms it by naming FL0160000 'Jacksonville Sheriff's Office'. The 25,684.75 hist_median fill must be dropped in full — it is the same agency's own 2019-2020 history being resurrected and double-counted against its successor's live report. The correct 2024 value for Jacksonville city (place 1235000) is the single live agency's figure alone: 33,545 under the SPUB lane preference the estimator already applied (32,309 if FBI lanes are preferred), and under no circumstance the 59,230 sum. This one case removes the 77% inflation on a ~1M-population place, which is why it is the highest-mass single defect in the screen.

verdict: defunct_no_fill — municipality dissolved; no Cahokia Heights successor ORI present in the supplied evidence
rationale: Cahokia village ceased to exist on 6 May 2021 when it merged with Alorton and Centreville into the city of Cahokia Heights, which matches IL0820300's last usable year (2020) and its roster absence exactly; the same applies to sibling IL0820500 CENTREVILLE (274.4 fill). Neither the successor ORI nor the Cahokia Heights place appears in the evidence given, so I name no successor — and the 656.8 hist_median must be dropped regardless, because it is keyed to place 1710370, a Census place that no longer exists, and drawn from a department that lost roughly half its officers in the transition. WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN TO THE TERRITORY: retire places 1710370 and 1712203, re-key the geography to the post-2021 Cahokia Heights place code, and route the ~14,000 residents (~17,000 across all three predecessors) through the benchmark-constrained silent-territory path in src/crimerisk/benchmark_imputation.py — this is precisely the Class A case that path was promoted for, and it carries explicit imputation provenance and uncertainty rather than laundering a dissolved agency's stale median as an observation. That path's own stated precondition ('verify each silent PD was active and primary — dead/contract/consolidated/sheriff-overlap check') is satisfied by this ruling: consolidated, not silent-but-active. Note the Illinois caveat — IL's historically poor FBI participation means a live Cahokia Heights PD may simply not report, so absence of a successor ORI is weak evidence about the successor department's existence.

verdict: plausibly_active (extant, non-reporting) — but no_fill; record as a coverage gap
rationale: EXPLICIT ANSWER TO THE TEST: no, 'absent from the FBI CDE 2024 roster' cannot be used as a proxy for 'defunct'. MBTA Transit Police is a large, unambiguously operating agency policing the Boston subway, bus and commuter-rail network; roster absence and panel silence are reporting-status facts, and conflating them with existence is precisely the inferential error that produced the fill in the first place. The correct move is to decouple two decisions the current logic has fused: (1) is the agency extant, and (2) may we fabricate a value. Extancy never licenses a hist_median fill. Here the fill fails on both independent grounds — a 2018-2019 base is structurally invalid for 2024 transit crime after the ridership collapse and partial recovery that intervened, and 25:statewide_overlap_layer w=1 with the county sentinel place 99025 smears station-level Boston-metro incidents across all of Massachusetts, on territory already covered by the municipal agencies whose boundaries contain those stations, creating a double-count on top of the fabrication. Correct disposition: drop the 426.6, mark MA013BA00 active-but-non-reporting so it is NOT swept up by any defunct-drop rule, and record the gap. If the product later needs the mass, it must come through the benchmark-constrained path with a real footprint (station geography or served municipalities), never from the agency's own stale median. GENERAL RULE: hist_median fill requires BOTH a recency condition (a usable observation within ~2 years) AND a valid non-overlay footprint; MBTA fails both, and the current estimator enforces neither.

verdict: defunct_no_fill — merged into York County Regional Police Department (successor ORI not present in the supplied evidence)
rationale: York Area Regional PD merged with Northeastern Regional PD to form York County Regional PD effective 1 January 2022 under ordinances approved 16 August 2021, which is consistent with the 2020 last-usable year and the 2024 roster absence; the FBIpop series running to 58,111 in 2022 with no counts is just the FBI carrying a population figure for a non-reporting ORI and is not evidence of activity. The 534.6 hist_median is dropped. I do not name a successor ORI because the merger could have been effected either as a new ORI or as Northeastern Regional's ORI relabelled, and neither is in evidence — resolve it by searching PA county 133 for a 2024-roster ORI named 'YORK COUNTY REGIONAL' whose population approximates the two predecessors combined. FOOTPRINT — the substantive half: 42:statewide_overlap_layer w=1 is the worst available answer, because it dilutes a 58,111-population suburban department across 13M Pennsylvanians, erasing the local signal and laying a uniform false floor statewide. A multi-municipality regional department does not need a single Census place; it needs a MULTI-ROW crosswalk — one row per member municipality (East Manchester Township, Windsor Township, York Township; plus Spring Garden Township from 1 June 2025), as PA county subdivisions/MCDs, population-weighted to sum to 1. That is exactly what the 99991 sentinel should trigger; falling through to the statewide overlay instead is the actual bug, and it will recur for every regional PD in PA, MI, and NY until the sentinel routes to MCD-set resolution rather than to fallback.

verdict: defunct_no_fill for the ORI (station itself active; successor ORI not identifiable from the supplied evidence)
rationale: FAMILY DECISION, consistent with a3-PA-statepolice-york: do NOT decide by ORI family. York proves PAPSP#### and PA###SP are DUPLICATE representations of the same PSP station reporting identical numbers, and it proves the live-vs-dead assignment flips between families station by station (York: PAPSP live, PA###SP dead; Erie: PAPSP dead). The rule is therefore per-station, not per-family: keep exactly the one counterpart that is on the 2024 roster AND carries 2024 data, drop the other, and fill neither — summing both double-counts, which is the live hazard the York case exposes. PAPSP2500 is off the roster with nothing since 2021, so the 1,218.9 hist_median off a two-year base is dropped; if no live Erie counterpart exists in the panel, that is a coverage gap to record, not a licence to fabricate. EVIDENCE THAT WOULD FIX A SUCCESSOR: match candidates on (a) station-name string, (b) county_fips 049, (c) near-identical offense vectors in any overlap year — the York signature, and the single strongest test, (d) 2024 roster presence with a coverage/nibrs_start date, cross-checked against (e) PSP's own published station roster or the PA UCR program's station-level table. FOOTPRINT, separately: 42:statewide_overlap_layer w=1 is wrong for every member of this family — a PSP station polices the municipalities in its county that have no local PD, so the correct footprint is the Erie County non-municipal/no-local-PD remainder, not all 13M Pennsylvanians.
